messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P1 — continuous-batcher queue depth spike in runtime-prod-uswest-2. Error rate rising, repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Alert ID PAG-20260309-001

alice: oncall here — seeing a rapid increase in batch queue length and latency. digging into logs now.

alice: tailing batcher logs, primary error is CUDA allocation failures followed by container restart loop.

ben: i'm on GPU metrics. node gpu-7 showing repeated page faults and kernel messages about GPU resets.

carmen: tagging eng-sre to help with node-level stability. runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/batching-paging

ben: sample from batcher logs:
```
E0309 14:02:12.123 batcher.go:412] cuda: allocation failed: out of memory (cudaMalloc). pid=2345 model=redwood-llama-13b seq=2048 batch=64
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
goroutine 58 [running]:
...stack trace...
```

dave: AtlasPayments (customer) reporting elevated latencies and 504s. they say the spike started ~14:01 UTC. pinged CS.

alice: customer impact confirmed: ~2-3% requests 5xx; p95 latency jumped from ~120ms to 3.4s for some routes. will throttle non-critical traffic.

alice: immediate mitigations I'm going to apply:
- reduce continuous-batcher.max_batch_size from 128 -> 32
- disable kv-prefetch (set kv_prefetch=false)
- route premium customers to cpu-fallback pool
- cordon and drain node gpu-7

ben: applied max_batch_size change and disabled prefetch via runtime-config. canary rolling out.

ops-bot: Deploy started by ben at 2026-03-09T14:08:05Z. Job ID: deploy-9843. Rolling update of batcher pods to config v2.

carmen: initiating k8s drain on gpu-7. will watch for pod restarts and ensure we don't cascade.

eve: looping in CS — will prepare a short customer note.

alice: short blurb for AtlasPayments: "We observed an internal batching runtime memory saturation causing increased latency and some timeouts. We've applied config limits, drained the affected node, and routed traffic to fallback pools. We'll follow up with a full RCA."

ben: found a deadlock/starvation pattern in the continuous-batcher: when prefetch eviction runs concurrently with enqueue a waiter can be left blocked and the flush path doesn't trigger, causing unbounded queue growth. crafting a quick patch to force wakeups on enqueue.

ben: patch excerpt:
```
diff --git a/batcher/queue.go b/batcher/queue.go
+    // ensure flushers don't starve if prefetch evictions race with enqueue
+    cond.Broadcast() // wake waiting flushers on enqueue
```

alice: applying patch to canary pods. if canary stable for ~2m we'll roll to the rest of the cluster.

incident-bot: [INCIDENT NOTE] PD incident PD-3421 created. Customer "AtlasPayments" escalated to SEV1 contact.

dave: Atlas on-call confirmed intermittent 502s. appreciate the fast response.

ben: canary looks good — queue depths are returning to normal, no new OOMs on canary pods. p95 for canary traffic ~220ms.

alice: rolling patch to prod but throttling to 2 pods at a time.

ops-bot: Rollout completed at 2026-03-09T14:24:01Z. Job ID: deploy-9843. No new crashes observed in last 8m.

carmen: drain of gpu-7 complete; replacing node with fresh instance. monitoring kernel logs for GPU pagefault patterns; collecting dmesg + nvidia logs.

ben: adding temporary LB throttle to keep continuous-batcher at <=80% capacity to avoid relapse while autoscaling stabilizes.

eve: CS sent initial status to AtlasPayments: "Mitigation in place; next update in 30m; incident lead: alice."

alice: drafting postmortem checklist and follow-ups:
- root cause hypothesis: unbounded batch growth + prefetch eviction race -> waiter starvation -> batcher memory spike -> CUDA OOM -> container crash -> node flaps under restart storm
- immediate follow-ups: revert/soften prefetch defaults, add enqueue wakeup test, add integration test for batcher under eviction, add autoscaling buffer for batcher pools
- longer term: improve kv cache eviction heuristics, per-batch memory accounting, and better tracing for batch lifecycle

carmen: SRE action items: bump node auto-replace threshold, alert on consecutive pod restarts >3 in 5m, include kernel OOM logs in incident bundles.

ben: note — one node showed "container runtime killed process 1 with signal 9" in syslog; likely host-level OOM kill from overcommit. collecting oom_kill logs.

alice: handing off to night oncall eve in 30m. changing incident status to monitoring; will keep RCA work moving.

eve: acknowledged. i'll watch for regressions and keep CS looped. escalate to eng-runtime + eng-sre if any new OOMs or node flaps.

ops-bot: Incident PD-3421 status updated to monitoring by alice at 2026-03-09T14:38:12Z.

carmen: notes for postmortem: include mem profiles, batch-size histograms, and timeline of node restarts + config changes (with deploy IDs).

eve: taking over at 2026-03-09T14:42:03Z. moving to monitoring.

alice: thanks all. filing follow-up tickets and will own RCA document.

End of thread.
